Comment.MultiLanguageText: The hand/auto selector position. NEVER WRITTEN BY THIS BLOCK - the caller or HMI owns it. It selects which command source the start rung follows (N1), its DESELECTION resets both hand latches (N2), it arms the start-signal re-assert timer (N3), it is edge-detected in BOTH directions to drop the prestart hold (N4/N5), it holds the upstream-enable timer off while it is set AND a hand intervention is active (N11), and it reaches the status code (N13).

The run command from the automatic source. Never written by this block, and read in exactly one place - the start rung (N1) - where it is the command source whenever the motor is not being driven by a hand intervention.

The run command from the operator side. THE BLOCK ONLY EVER RESETS IT (RCOIL in N2 on any of hand deselected, no hand intervention, fault active or motor inhibited; and RCOIL in N3 once the 100 ms re-assert timer has expired) AND NEVER SETS IT: the set belongs to the HMI, which N2's own network comment states as a wiring contract. It is therefore a momentary press latched outside the block, not a maintained command. Read by the start rung (N1), the re-assert timer (N3) and the shutdown-complete rung (N7).

The running feedback - contactor auxiliary, rotation sensor, whatever the instance is wired to. Never written by this block. Its DISAGREEMENT with the commanded state is what the two fail-to detections time out on (N8/N9); its agreement is what qualifies the upstream enable (N11) and the hours totaliser (N12); and N7 requires it clear before a shutdown counts as complete.

An external fault about this motor that the block cannot detect itself. THE BLOCK ONLY RESETS IT (RCOIL on FaultReset, N10) and never sets it, so this member has two writers - the external detector and this block - unlike FTR and FTS, which the block owns outright. It ORs into FaultActive (N10) and is published on alarm bit 2 (N14).

The permissive that must be present for this motor to be commanded at all. Never written by this block, and read in exactly one place - the start rung (N1). Nothing about what makes the system healthy is decided here.

The prestart sequence for this motor has completed. Never written by this block. It sets the prestart hold (N5), and its ABSENCE while that hold is up and hand is selected is what the 30 s prestart-timeout timer times (N4), that timeout then dropping the hold again. What prestart consists of is the caller's business; the block sees only the completion bit.

A hard inhibit from outside - isolator, zone trip, process interlock, anything. Never written by this block. It drops the start rung (N1) and forces the hand-start reset (N2). No source is named or assumed here; an interlock that must see other equipment is computed by whoever owns that equipment and arrives on this one bit.

Clears the latched faults. Never written by this block. It breaks the seal-in of FTR (N8), FTS (N9) and FaultActive (N10), and resets FaultFB (N10). A fault whose cause is still true re-latches on the same scan through its own detection term, so this delivers clear every latched fault WHOSE CAUSE HAS GONE without any comparison logic.

SECONDS. The fail-to time, SHARED BY BOTH DETECTIONS - N6 converts it once into FTTimeMS and both the fail-to-run timer (N8) and the fail-to-stop timer (N9) use that single preset, so the two cannot be tuned apart. Held in seconds for operator legibility and multiplied by 1000 into the DInt millisecond preset the timers actually take (N6).
SECONDS. How long the motor must be commanded AND confirmed running before UPSEnable is published (N11). Converted once into EnableUPSTimeMS in N6, same x1000 idiom as the other two times.

THE ONE FAULT BIT THE REST OF THE BLOCK READS, never the individual causes: FTR OR FTS OR FaultFB, sealed in and cleared only by FaultReset (N10). It drops the start rung (N1), forces the hand start command off (N2), drops the recent-start memory (N3) and the prestart hold (N5), completes a shutdown outright (N7) and sets the status code to -1 (N13). Written only in N10.

THE COMMANDED RUN STATE, and the member an output mapping should read. Written only in N1, where the initiate branch needs TryRunMotor with the prestart hold and a recent start, the seal-in branch needs only TryRunMotor, and StopMotor or Shutdown drops both. Everything downstream keys off it: both fail-to detections (N8/N9), the upstream enable (N11), the hours totaliser (N12) and the status code (N13).

The C-115 handshake out: this motor has been confirmed running for EnableUPSTime, so whatever it enables may run. Written in N11 as a direct UNLATCHED follow of the enable timer's Q, so it drops the moment the run confirmation does. The only reader inside this block is the status code (N13) - its real consumer is the next equipment's own start permission, which is outside this block and cannot be seen from here.

FAIL TO RUN. LATCHED CAUSE, alarm bit 0 - commanded to run with no running feedback, continuously for longer than FTTime (N8). Seals itself in at its own detection network and clears only on FaultReset. Feeds FaultActive (N10) and is published unlatched on Alarm bit 0 (N14). It fires on positive evidence of the wrong state; it never proves the motor IS running.

FAIL TO STOP. LATCHED CAUSE, alarm bit 1 - not commanded to run while the running feedback is still made, continuously for longer than the SAME FTTime (N9). Same seal-in and same reset as FTR. Feeds FaultActive (N10) and Alarm bit 1 (N14).

The running-hours totaliser. WHAT N12 CONTAINS: a retentive one-hour timer over commanded-and-confirmed running, self-reset by its own Q, an ADD of 1 into this member guarded by that Q AND NOT RisingEdgeFlags[2], and a MOVE of 0 taking the ADD's place at 4294967295 - so the INTENDED behaviour is one count per hour, rolling over rather than saturating. THE INTENTION IS STATED SEPARATELY FROM THE BEHAVIOUR ON PURPOSE, because the two may not agree: the coil that writes RisingEdgeFlags[2] from Q sits BEFORE the MOVE and the ADD that test NOT RisingEdgeFlags[2] in that same network, which on the IR's documented same-scan freshness rule makes the guard false exactly when Q is true, and neither the increment nor the rollover could then fire. Two independent blind review runs recorded that same reading against the same network shape in the fwd/rev sibling block (docs/evidence/review-simplicity-blind-run-2026-07-16.md, review-conventions-blind-run-2026-07-16.md item 7a), both flagging it to be CONFIRMED IN TIA rather than acted on. Left exactly as found - this is proven site code and the ruling is the owner's. Written only in N12 and read nowhere else in this block. The member's mechanism also carries the block's known C-406 deviation - N12 uses TONR directly, which the rule bans; pattern.md documents it as real existing content, not as the shape to copy.

One status code for the operator display, written in N13 as a chain of overriding MOVEs, last enabled wins: 0 stopped, 1 commanded to run, 2 confirmed running, 3 confirmed running with either the upstream enable made or hand selected, -1 faulted. Written only in N13 and read nowhere else in this block. Adding a state is one more MOVE line rather than a re-cut of a comparison tree.

THE ALARM WORD, WRITTEN IN ONE NETWORK (N14): bit 0 FTR, bit 1 FTS, bit 2 FaultFB. Each bit is a DIRECT UNLATCHED read of an already-latched cause, so the word inherits latched behaviour rather than implementing it, and the block never reads this word back. THE BLOCK WRITES BITS 0 TO 2 AND NOTHING ELSE - bits 3 to 15 belong to the application, which allocates and writes them itself. KNOWN GAP, RECORDED RATHER THAN FIXED: N14 carries no bit-map network comment, which C-501 condition 3 now requires; that condition postdates this proven site block, so it is written up in pattern.md and left for the owner rather than edited in.

NO READER AND NO WRITER ANYWHERE IN THIS BLOCK. None of the fourteen networks touches this member - not the status code, not the alarm word, not a rung condition - so what consumes it CANNOT BE DETERMINED FROM THE LADDER, only that this block does not. What can be said as fact: the committed example instance DB gives it a descriptive equipment label as its download value (examples/MotorStarterInst8.ir), which is consistent with a panel-side label but is an inference from one start value and not something the block demonstrates. WORTH KNOWING BEFORE COPYING: under C-132 the whole struct is instantiated RETAIN, so a String here is retentive memory on every instance for something no logic in this block uses.

The operator has taken this motor in hand at the HMI. THE BLOCK ONLY EVER RESETS IT (RCOIL when hand is deselected, N2) and never sets it - the same HMI set contract as HandStartSignal, stated in N2's own network comment. Read by the start rung, where InHand AND this bit together are what switch the command source from auto to hand (N1), by the shutdown-complete rung (N7), and by the upstream-enable timer (N11), which does not run while both are set.

A start has recently been commanded at the HMI. THE BLOCK NEVER SETS IT EITHER: N3's coil is a HOLD-ONLY term - RecentStart AND NOT Run AND PreStartMemory AND NOT FaultActive - so the block can only maintain or drop it, and the set is the HMI's per N3's own network comment. It gates the INITIATE branch of the Run rung (N1), which the seal-in branch then bypasses once running, and it conditions the re-assert timer (N3).

The arbitrated run REQUEST, one network before the run itself: the selected command source - auto, or hand where a hand intervention is active - ANDed with no inhibit, no active fault and system healthy (N1). Written only in N1. Its readers in this block are the Run rung in that same network and the re-assert timer's condition (N3); whether any caller reads it cannot be told from inside the block.

A controlled-shutdown request from the caller. Never written by this block. Its RISING EDGE sets StopMotor (N7, edge constructed against a stored bit per C-404) and while it remains present the StopMotor reset is held off; it also drops the Run rung directly (N1), so the run stops on the request and the timer below governs only when the shutdown is declared complete.

The controlled shutdown has finished. Written in N7 with its own seal-in (held while Run is clear) by any of three things: the shutdown timer expiring with the running feedback gone, hand selected with a hand intervention and no hand start command, or an active fault. Read in N7 to release StopMotor; no other reader inside this block, and pattern.md records that neighbouring equipment's shutdown sequencing consumes it.

SECONDS. How long the motor is given to come to rest after StopMotor is set before the timer half of the shutdown-complete condition is satisfied (N7). Converted once into ShutdownTimeMS in N6. Note that expiry alone is not enough - the running feedback must also be gone.

The stop that carries out a controlled shutdown. THE BLOCK OWNS BOTH EDGES: set in N7 on the rising edge of Shutdown, reset in N7 once ShutdownComplete is up and Shutdown has gone - so it is published state rather than a caller input, despite sitting among the commands. It drops the Run rung (N1) and is the input the shutdown timer times (N7).

AttributeList.Text: THE COMPLETE CALLER-VISIBLE INTERFACE OF MotorStarter - commands, feedbacks, commissioning times, published state, latched faults and the alarm word, all of it, in one type. C-132: an FB's entire interface is ONE STATIC member of its own interface UDT, and an equipment FB declares no INPUT, OUTPUT or IN_OUT parameters at all - MotorStarter's own INPUT and OUTPUT sections are empty and the whole interface is IO : MotorIOSet RETAIN SETPOINT. The instance DB therefore IS the interface: the caller writes into it, the panel binds to it (C-503), and retention is declared at the FB static that instantiates it, which is the only place retention CAN be stated - a TYPE member carries no Remanence attribute in the real XML shape, so a RETAIN token on a member line here would be silently dropped crossing to XML (FI-47). NO MEMBER BELOW CARRIES RETAIN, DELIBERATELY. PROVENANCE, BECAUSE IT MATTERS FOR HOW MUCH THIS FILE PROVES: the member list is recovered from MotorStarter.ir's own STATIC section, where IO carries its members as inline nested declarations - it is NOT a fresh export of a real PLC data type. The real project's type is TypeDOL; MotorIOSet is the sanitized/committed name that MotorStarter.ir and examples/MotorStarterInst8.ir both already reference, so the names and the order here are the block's own, member for member. Start values are omitted: the block's inline declaration carries none, and the per-instance download values live on the instance DB (examples/MotorStarterInst8.ir). DIRECTION IS NOT DECLARED ANYWHERE ON A TYPE - there are no input and output sections to sort these into - so each member's comment states who writes it and who reads it, as observed in this block's ladder. THE COMMENTS ARE WRITTEN FROM THE LADDER AND FROM NOTHING ELSE. The site block carries no member comments of its own, so every statement below is one that MotorStarter's fourteen networks demonstrate; where the ladder shows nothing, the comment says so rather than offering a plausible sentence - see Name, which no network in this block touches at all. Network numbers are cited as N1..N14 throughout so any claim can be checked against the rung that makes it.
